messages.subject: assert triggers in irace 2.2
parts:
We have probably found a bug in irace 2.2 using R 3.2.3. In two projects of us each time after the second of three iterations completes the irace.assert(sum(nrow(iraceResults$experimentLog)) == experimentsUsedSoFar) fails within the irace function. In both cases batchmode has been set to sge and we used adapted target-runner and target-evaluators as in the example example.

We found that this assert was not present in irace 2.1. The rdata file written by irace is still in the state when iteration two starts. Here is the output of the irace run:

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] assert triggers in irace 2.2
parts:
Dear Johannes,

Thanks for reporting this. The assert is detecting that the elements in
experimentLog are more than the number of experiments executed. I have now
analyzed that this happens because we record in experimentLog experiments that
are actually not executed (because they are elitist and we re-use a previous
result). I have long suspected this may be the case when target-evaluator is
used (since target-evaluator is always invoked but target-runner is sometimes
not if we have already done the same experiment), but I couldn't reproduce it,
so thanks again for reporting this.

For the final user, the only thing wrong is the data structure experimentLog,
which is just a log and not really used by irace for computations or deciding
when to stop. Thus, if you don't use this log for further analysis, you may
simply comment out the assert. You may also downgrade to irace 2.1, but
experimentLog may also be wrong there.

I'm preparing a more thorough fix so that experimentLog is correct, but it may
take some days to reach CRAN.

Best wishes,

Manuel.
